description: Claim payment amount is materially higher than peers for similar claim profiles.
business_reason: Large paid amounts can indicate inflated reimbursement requests or billing errors.

description: Submitted charge amount is in the extreme upper tail of observed claims.
business_reason: Very high submitted charges may represent overpricing, duplicate billing, or unsupported services.

description: Submitted line charge is disproportionately high versus allowed charge.
business_reason: A high submitted-to-allowed ratio suggests persistent overbilling pressure on adjudication.

description: Submitted line charge is abnormally high relative to actual Medicare payment.
business_reason: A large gap between submitted and paid values can signal systematic billing inflation.

description: Service count is high relative to diagnosis complexity.
business_reason: Utilization out of proportion to clinical complexity can indicate unnecessary service volume.

description: Diagnosis count exceeds typical claim burden.
business_reason: Overly dense diagnosis coding may indicate coding inflation to justify higher utilization.

description: Claim-level submitted charges materially exceed claim-level allowed charges.
business_reason: Large claim-level gaps can indicate billing amounts not aligned with payer fee schedules.

description: Billing behavior appears elevated versus specialty-specific peers.
business_reason: Relative outlier billing among same-specialty providers can indicate coding at higher-paying levels.

description: Line-level service volume is in the top distribution tail.
business_reason: Excess utilization can suggest unbundling or medically unnecessary repeated services.

description: Multiple monetary fields simultaneously fall in extreme percentiles.
business_reason: Concurrent high-end financial indicators often warrant immediate audit prioritization.

description: Provider submitted amount is significantly above specialty median.
business_reason: Deviation from specialty baseline may indicate non-standard charging practices.

description: Allowed amounts do not align with paid amounts at expected levels.
business_reason: Inconsistent allowed-versus-paid behavior can indicate billing workflow anomalies.

description: Atypical concentration of high-value line charges in a single claim.
business_reason: High concentration patterns can point to charge stacking or non-random billing behavior.

description: Claims show substantial submitted charges despite low or zero net payment.
business_reason: This pattern may indicate repeated non-payable submissions or intentional charge inflation.

description: Service and charge intensity is elevated compared with providers in the same specialty.
business_reason: Specialty-relative outliers can identify aberrant practice styles needing targeted review.

description: Claim breaches multiple anomaly indicators across finance and utilization dimensions.
business_reason: Multi-signal anomalies generally carry higher fraud risk than isolated single-feature outliers.

description: Submitted amounts rise steeply versus expected adjudicated values.
business_reason: Escalation trends can indicate deliberate billing inflation over realistic reimbursement levels.

description: Service volume does not scale consistently with diagnosis burden.
business_reason: Mismatch between diagnoses and performed services can indicate unnecessary procedures.

description: Coding and monetary profile imply higher-than-expected claim complexity.
business_reason: Inflated severity coding can increase reimbursement and should be clinically validated.

description: Financial values cluster near historical extremes in one claim event.
business_reason: Extreme-value clustering is uncommon and useful for prioritizing investigative queues.

description: Claim appears within a pattern of high-cost billing signals.
business_reason: Repeated high-cost anomalies may indicate persistent billing control weaknesses or abusive behavior.
